rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with front matter (`name: habeas`), so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions`.

The requirement has one obligation for each site. The description MUST state when to use the skill in terms of the user's task. It MAY name another bundled skill where an agent could confuse the two.

The `description` field in the front matter begins "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas…". That states a trigger in terms of the user's task, which is any work in a Habeas-tracking project. It also lists concrete signals: a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references. It then says what the skill is for, which is picking the task skill (`habeas-requirements`, `habeas-refactor`, `habeas-evidence`, `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`), and it names the syntax and `habeas status`/`habeas info` reference content. Naming the other bundled skills is allowed by the MAY and imposes nothing to check.

One could argue the trigger is phrased in terms of the project's state rather than a task. The "start of any work" wording is task-oriented, though, so I find no gap.

The inputs list no violation-query matches to judge.
